mainTopic: The years of שילה, the source for במות at נוב וגבעון, מעשר שני in that period, and the meaning of מנוחה and נחלה
overview: This amud finishes a count of years. Verses about דוד and שלמה complete the 57 years of נוב וגבעון, and that leaves 369 years for שילה. The גמרא then asks for the source that במות were allowed in the time of נוב וגבעון. It finds the source in the פסוק 'the rest and the inheritance': the time between the two places was a time when במות were permitted. ריש לקיש asks why the משנה leaves out מעשר שני for נוב וגבעון. רבי יוחנן first ties מעשר שני to the ארון. When ריש לקיש pushes back, רבי יוחנן says instead that the משנה follows רבי שמעון. According to רבי יהודה, מעשר שני was eaten at נוב וגבעון, which counted as a בירה. Finally, the גמרא brings four views on which places the words מנוחה and נחלה refer to. It defends the order of the words for רבי שמעון, and it begins a new question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: דוד's reign proves part of the נוב וגבעון years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק that דוד ruled forty years, seven in חברון and thirty-three in ירושלים. This supports its count of the years the משכן stood in נוב וגבעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'The days that דוד ruled over Israel were forty years. In חברון he ruled seven years,' and the verse goes on to say thirty-three years in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of adding up the 57 years of נוב וגבעון. Here it brings a פסוק to show how many years דוד ruled in ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארון stayed in קרית יערים for 20 years, until דוד brought it to ירושלים. דוד then ruled another 33 years in ירושלים. All that time the משכן was still in נוב וגבעון, so 20 + 33 = 53 years so far.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written; introduces a פסוק as a source
Ruled, reigned as king
חברון, the city where דוד first ruled
Short for וגומר, 'and so on'; the פסוק continues

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The step begins with 'דכתיב' because it continues a count of years that started before this section.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And the days that David reigned'
over Israel were forty years;
in Hebron he reigned seven years, etc.'
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the פסוק: thirty-three years in ירושלים. That's the number the גמרא needs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the count of years from the earlier discussion, before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד ruled 33 years in ירושלים, which counts toward the נוב וגבעון period

steps.title: שלמה began building in his fourth year
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says שלמה started building the בית המקדש in the fourth year of his reign. This finishes the 57 years of נוב וגבעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: About שלמה it is written: 'He began to build it in the fourth year of his reign.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the last piece of the count: the years of שלמה's reign before the building began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 53 years from the step before, plus 4 years of שלמה, equals 57 years. That is how long the משכן stood in נוב וגבעון. Once the בית המקדש stood in ירושלים, that period was over.

keyTerms.meaning: King שלמה, son of דוד, who built the first בית המקדש
And he began to build it
His reign, his kingship

phrases.english: And regarding Solomon it is written:
'And he began to build it
in the fourth year of his reign.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the last 4 years to the count started with דוד.
steps.raayaObject: The 4 years of שלמה before building, which complete the 57 years of נוב וגבעון

steps.title: שילה stood for 369 years
steps.stepSummary: After subtracting all the other periods, the גמרא concludes that the משכן stood in שילה for 370 years minus one, which is 369.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is left for שילה is three hundred seventy years minus one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the math and gives the final number of years for שילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From leaving מצרים until the building of the בית המקדש was 480 years. Take away 40 years in the desert, 14 in גלגל, and 57 in נוב וגבעון, which is 111 years. That leaves 369 for שילה.

keyTerms.meaning: There remain; what is left over
שילה, where the משכן stood longest
Minus one

steps.whatToRemember: The משכן's travels: desert 40 years, גלגל 14, שילה 369, נוב וגבעון 57. Together they add up to 480 years, until שלמה began the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: There remain for Shiloh
three hundred and seventy less one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the completed 57-year count to work out the years of שילה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משכן stood in שילה for 369 years.

steps.title: What is the source that במות were allowed in נוב וגבעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line in the משנה about arriving at נוב וגבעון. It asks how we know that במות became permitted then.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'They came to נוב וגבעון,' and so on. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה. It asks for the source of the rule, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that after שילה was destroyed and the משכן moved to נוב וגבעון, private במות were allowed again. The גמרא wants a source in the תורה for that change.

keyTerms.meaning: נוב and גבעון, the places where the משכן stood after שילה
Short for וכולי, 'and so on'
From where are these matters known? A request for the source

phrases.english: They came to Nov and Gibeon, etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the count of years and turns to the next law in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that במות were permitted during the time of נוב וגבעון

steps.title: 'Rest' is שילה and 'inheritance' is ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק 'you have not yet come to the rest and to the inheritance.' It explains that 'rest' means שילה and 'inheritance' means ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'For you have not yet come to the rest and to the inheritance.' 'The rest' is שילה. 'The inheritance' is ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The ברייתא reads the פסוק as naming two different places where the משכן would rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says במות are allowed until you reach 'the rest and the inheritance.' The ברייתא matches each word to a place: 'rest' is שילה and 'inheritance' is ירושלים. This prepares the next question: why does the פסוק name two places?

keyTerms.meaning: Rest; here it means שילה
Inheritance; here it means ירושלים

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
'For you have not yet come until now
to the rest and to the inheritance';
'To the rest' – this is Shiloh,
'inheritance' – this is Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק names two places, 'rest' (שילה) and 'inheritance' (ירושלים).

steps.title: Why does the פסוק name them separately?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק splits the two places into two separate words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did the פסוק divide them?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a short question about the wording of the פסוק. This sets up the key teaching in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have used one word for the place where במות stop. The ברייתא assumes that naming two places must teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: Why did it divide them?

phrases.english: Why did it divide them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the two-place reading from the step before.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What we learn from the פסוק naming 'rest' and 'inheritance' as two separate things

steps.title: The time between שילה and ירושלים allowed במות
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק separates the two places to teach that in the time between שילה and ירושלים, במות were permitted. That time was the period of נוב וגבעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It divided them to give permission for במות in the time between this one and that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the answer, and this is the source for the rule in the משנה. The time between שילה and ירושלים, which was נוב וגבעון, was a time when במות were allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each place, 'rest' and 'inheritance,' made במות forbidden while the משכן or בית המקדש was there. By naming them separately, the פסוק shows a gap between them. During that gap, which was נוב וגבעון, private במות were permitted again.

keyTerms.meaning: Permission; here, permission to use במות
Between this one and that one; the time between שילה and ירושלים
A private altar, set up outside the משכן or בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: 'Rest' is שילה and 'inheritance' is ירושלים. The פסוק names them separately, so the time between them, נוב וגבעון, was a time when במות were permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the תורה source behind the משנה's rule. It explains why במות were allowed in some periods of history and forbidden in others.

phrases.english: In order to give permission
between this one and that one.
phrases.notes: The time between שילה and ירושלים, which was the period of נוב וגבעון.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן הֶיתֵּר בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about why the פסוק divides the two places, and so finishes the source for the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because the פסוק separates 'rest' and 'inheritance,' במות were permitted during the time between שילה and ירושלים, the time of נוב וגבעון.

steps.title: Why doesn't the משנה mention מעשר שני at נוב וגבעון?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks רבי יוחנן why the משנה does not also list מעשר שני for the period of נוב וגבעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: The משנה should also teach the law of מעשר שני!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש points out that something seems to be missing from the משנה: it does not say where מעשר שני was eaten in the time of נוב וגבעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שילה, the משנה said that קדשים קלים and מעשר שני were eaten anywhere you could see שילה. For נוב וגבעון it only mentions קדשים קלים. ריש לקיש wants to know why מעשר שני dropped out.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe of produce, which must be eaten in the holy place
Let it teach / it should have taught

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan:
Let [the Mishnah] teach second tithe as well!
phrases.notes: For שילה the משנה mentioned מעשר שני, but for נוב וגבעון it left it out. That gap is what bothers him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the משנה's list of what was eaten at נוב וגבעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה about נוב וגבעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה mentioned מעשר שני for שילה, so leaving it out for נוב וגבעון looks like a gap.

steps.title: מעשר שני depends on the ארון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that מעשר שני is learned from the ארון through the word 'שם'. Since the ארון was not at נוב וגבעון, מעשר שני was not eaten there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: מעשר is learned from the ארון through the word 'שם' that appears in both places. Since the ארון was not there, מעשר was not eaten there either.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains why the משנה left out מעשר שני: it simply was not eaten at נוב וגבעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה links the word 'שם' written about מעשר to the word 'שם' written about the ארון. So מעשר שני can only be eaten where the ארון is. At נוב וגבעון the ארון was somewhere else, so there was no eating of מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: A link between two topics based on a shared word in the פסוקים
The Holy Ark
They learn it out / derive it

phrases.english: He said to him:
Tithe — they learn it from the Ark, through 'there'–'there';
phrases.notes: The word 'שם' shows up for מעשר (דברים 12:7) and for the ארון (שמות 40:3).

phrases.english: since the Ark was not there,
tithe also was not [eaten there].

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֵׂר שָׁם שָׁם מֵאָרוֹן קָא יָלְפִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's question by saying מעשר שני really was not eaten at נוב וגבעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The omission is correct, because the law did not apply then
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forgot to mention מעשר שני
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר שני needs the ארון, and the ארון was not at נוב וגבעון

steps.title: Then פסח and other offerings should also need the ארון
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש objects: פסח and קדשים also have the word 'שם', so by the same logic they should not have been brought at נוב וגבעון either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the קרבן פסח and other קדשים are also learned from the ארון through 'שם'–'שם'. Since the ארון was not there, they should not have been brought there either!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן's answer by showing it proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that פסח and קדשים were brought and eaten at נוב וגבעון. If the word 'שם' makes something depend on the ארון, those offerings should also have been impossible there. So the ארון reasoning cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
The Pesach offering
Sacrifices

phrases.english: If so,
the Pesach offering and other sacrifices too —
they are learned from the Ark through 'there'–'there';
so since the Ark was not there,
they too should not have been [brought]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word 'שם' appears for פסח and קדשים, yet they were brought at נוב וגבעון without the ארון.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a new answer: the משנה follows רבי שמעון, who says offerings without a fixed time, like מעשר בהמה, were not brought then. מעשר שני is linked to מעשר בהמה, so it was not eaten either.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The one who told you this, who is it? It is רבי שמעון, who says: Even the public offered only the פסח and required offerings with a fixed time. Required offerings with no fixed time were not offered on either kind of altar. מעשר בהמה is a required offering with no fixed time, and מעשר דגן is linked to מעשר בהמה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן drops the ארון reasoning and explains the משנה's omission in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, only offerings with a set time, like פסח, were brought in that period. מעשר בהמה has no set time, so it was not brought. Because the תורה links grain tithe (מעשר שני) to מעשר בהמה, מעשר שני was not eaten either.

keyTerms.meaning: Required offerings that have a fixed time
Animal tithe, every tenth animal, brought as an offering
Is linked by a היקש, a comparison in the פסוק
Grain tithe, meaning מעשר שני

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוחנן is defending his first answer. He is replacing the ארון reasoning with a completely different explanation.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The one who told you this, who is it?
phrases.notes: He means the משנה, which left out מעשר שני for נוב וגבעון.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Shimon, who says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף צִבּוּר לֹא הִקְרִיבוּ אֶלָּא פֶּסַח
phrases.english: Even the public offered only the Pesach
and required offerings that have a fixed time,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חוֹבוֹת שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לָהֶם זְמַן –
phrases.english: but required offerings that have no fixed time —
were not offered here or there.
phrases.notes: Neither on the big public altar nor on a private במה.

phrases.aramaic: מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה – חוֹבוֹת שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לָהֶן זְמַן הוּא,
phrases.english: Animal tithe is a required offering that has no fixed time,
and grain tithe is linked to animal tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲמַר לָךְ הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge in step 10 by giving a new reason for the omission in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The omission is explained by the ארון
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי שמעון: no מעשר בהמה then, so no מעשר שני either
steps.whyThisMatters: It means the omission of מעשר שני is not a universal rule. It depends on רבי שמעון's view, which opens the question of what רבי יהודה holds.

steps.title: So according to רבי יהודה, were they offered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether it follows that according to רבי יהודה, these offerings were brought at נוב וגבעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this imply that according to רבי יהודה they were offered?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the flip side. If the omission is only רבי שמעון's view, what does רבי יהודה say?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי שמעון about offerings with no fixed time. So the גמרא asks whether, in his view, מעשר בהמה was brought and מעשר שני eaten at נוב וגבעון.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication / does it follow
They were offered

phrases.english: Does this imply that according to Rabbi Yehuda they were offered?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the attribution to רבי שמעון in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה holds that מעשר בהמה and מעשר שני applied at נוב וגבעון

steps.title: Yes: רב אדא בר מתנה's statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes, quoting רב אדא בר מתנה that according to רבי יהודה, מעשר שני and מעשר בהמה were eaten at נוב וגבעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, for רב אדא בר מתנה said: מעשר שני and מעשר בהמה are eaten in נוב וגבעון according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא confirms the inference with a direct statement from an אמורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר מתנה says outright that in רבי יהודה's view both tithes were eaten at נוב וגבעון. This confirms the משנה's silence is only רבי שמעון's position.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Are eaten

phrases.aramaic: אִין; דְּהָאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה:
phrases.english: Yes, for Rav Adda bar Mattana said:
Second tithe and animal tithe
are eaten in Nov and Givon
according to Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין דְּהָאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. According to רבי יהודה, מעשר שני and מעשר בהמה were eaten at נוב וגבעון.

steps.title: But מעשר שני needs a permanent building
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: מעשר שני requires a בירה, and נוב וגבעון seems not to have one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it requires a בירה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אדא בר מתנה's statement, asking how מעשר שני could be eaten at נוב וגבעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that מעשר שני may only be eaten where there is a בירה. If נוב וגבעון did not count as one, then even רבי יהודה should not allow מעשר שני there.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent holy building / Temple
Requires

phrases.english: But it requires a 'birah'!
phrases.notes: A בירה here means the Temple building. The question assumes מעשר שני can only be eaten where there is one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר מתנה's statement that מעשר שני was eaten at נוב וגבעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעשר שני requires a בירה, and נוב וגבעון seemingly lacked one.

steps.title: רב יוסף: נוב וגבעון counted as a בירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by quoting רב יוסף's teaching that there were three בירות: שילה, נוב וגבעון, and the בית עולמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב יוסף teach: There are three בירות: שילה, נוב וגבעון, and the בית עולמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection by showing that נוב וגבעון did count as a בירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף lists נוב וגבעון together with שילה and the בית המקדש as a בירה. So the requirement of a בירה was met, and מעשר שני could be eaten there.

keyTerms.meaning: Plural of בירה
The eternal house, the בית המקדש in ירושלים

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yosef teach:
There are three 'birahs':
Shiloh, Nov and Givon, and the Eternal House?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף שָׁלֹשׁ בִּירוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the assumed missing condition was actually met
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נוב וגבעון was not a בירה
steps.terutzMaskana: נוב וגבעון was one of the three בירות

steps.title: רב יוסף's list is about eating מעשר שני, following רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב יוסף himself said his list of three בירות refers to eating מעשר שני, and follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He teaches it and he explains it: it is about eating מעשר שני, and it follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic by explaining what רב יוסף's teaching was about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף explained that 'three בירות' means three places fit for eating מעשר שני, and that this follows רבי יהודה. This fits exactly with רב אדא בר מתנה's statement, so everything lines up.

keyTerms.term: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He taught it and he himself explained it
According to the view of

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, מעשר שני was not eaten at נוב וגבעון, which is why the משנה leaves it out. According to רבי יהודה, it was eaten there, because נוב וגבעון counted as a בירה.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ:
phrases.english: He teaches it and he explains it:
it is about eating second tithe,
and it follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the scope of רב יוסף's teaching from step 15, tying it to רבי יהודה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: נוב וגבעון was a בירה for eating מעשר שני according to רבי יהודה. The משנה's silence reflects רבי שמעון.

steps.title: מנוחה means שילה and נחלה means ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and brings a ברייתא. In it, רבי יהודה explains that מנוחה in the פסוק is שילה and נחלה is ירושלים, and he brings two פסוקים where ירושלים is called 'My inheritance.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'They arrived at ירושלים, etc.' The רבנן taught in a ברייתא: 'For you have not yet come to the rest and to the inheritance.' 'Rest' is שילה, and 'inheritance' is ירושלים. Another פסוק says: 'My inheritance has become to Me like a lion in the forest.' Another פסוק says: 'Is My inheritance to Me a speckled bird of prey? Are birds of prey all around against her?' These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה ('they arrived at ירושלים'). It brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה explains which place the פסוק calls 'rest' and which it calls 'inheritance.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים names two stages: מנוחה and נחלה. רבי יהודה says the first stage, מנוחה, is שילה, and the second, נחלה, is ירושלים. His proof is that in ירמיהו, God calls ירושלים 'My inheritance.'

keyTerms.meaning: Rest, a resting place
Inheritance, a permanent possession
The city where the משכן stood for many years before the בית המקדש
A bird of prey

phrases.english: "They arrived at Jerusalem, etc."
The Rabbis taught:
"For you have not yet come until now
to the rest and to the inheritance."
"Rest": this is Shiloh;
"Inheritance": this is Jerusalem.
And it says: "My inheritance has become to Me
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 12:8. This is a prophecy about ירושלים that calls it 'My inheritance.'

phrases.english: like a lion in the forest."
And it says: "Is My inheritance to Me a speckled bird of prey?
Are birds of prey all around against her?"
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כִּי לֹא בָּאתֶם עַד עָתָּה אֶל הַמְּנוּחָה וְאֶל הַנַּחֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of בירות from steps 12-16 and opens a new section on the משנה's words 'they arrived at ירושלים.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, מנוחה is שילה and נחלה is ירושלים, because ירמיהו calls ירושלים God's 'inheritance.'

steps.title: מנוחה means ירושלים and נחלה means שילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reverses רבי יהודה's view. He says מנוחה is ירושלים and נחלה is שילה. His proof is a פסוק in תהלים that calls ציון God's 'resting place forever.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'Rest' is ירושלים, and 'inheritance' is שילה. A פסוק says: 'This is My resting place forever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it.' And another פסוק says: 'For ה' has chosen ציון; He desired it as His dwelling.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי יהודה and swaps the two places. He proves from תהלים that ירושלים is called God's 'resting place.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא finds a פסוק elsewhere in תנ״ך that attaches one of the words to ירושלים. רבי יהודה found ירושלים called נחלה, and רבי שמעון finds ירושלים (ציון) called מנוחה. The second פסוק, about ציון being chosen, shows that the 'resting place' in the first פסוק is ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Zion, another name for ירושלים
A dwelling place
I have desired it

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
"Rest": this is Jerusalem;
"Inheritance": this is Shiloh.
And it says: "This is My resting place forever;
here I will dwell, for I have desired it."
And it says: "For the Lord has chosen Zion;
phrases.notes: תהלים 132:13, the פסוק right before. It shows that the 'resting place' is ציון, meaning ירושלים.

phrases.english: He desired it as His dwelling."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מְנוּחָה זוֹ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, מנוחה is ירושלים and נחלה is שילה, because תהלים calls ציון God's 'resting place.'

steps.title: The verse's order seems wrong for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי יהודה's view fits the order of the פסוק, because שילה came first and then ירושלים. According to רבי שמעון, though, the פסוק should have said 'to the inheritance and to the rest.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says 'rest' is שילה, because that is why the פסוק says 'to the rest and to the inheritance.' But for the one who says 'rest' is ירושלים and 'inheritance' is שילה, the פסוק should have said 'to the inheritance and to the rest'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון from the order of the words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Historically, שילה came before ירושלים. רבי יהודה reads the פסוק in that time order: first rest (שילה), then inheritance (ירושלים). For רבי שמעון the פסוק would be naming ירושלים before שילה, which seems backward.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense; this opens a contrast that ends in a challenge
According to the one who says
It should have said

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
"rest" is Shiloh,
that is why it is written:
"to the rest and to the inheritance."
But according to the one who says
"rest" is Jerusalem and "inheritance" is Shiloh,
it should have said "to the inheritance and to the rest"!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְנוּחָה זוֹ שִׁילֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבי שמעון's view from step 18 against the order of the words in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's reading that מנוחה is ירושלים and נחלה is שילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק names מנוחה first. Since שילה came before ירושלים, the earlier place should be named first, so מנוחה should be שילה.

steps.title: Not even the lesser place has been reached
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that for רבי שמעון the פסוק is not listing the places by time. It builds from the bigger to the smaller: you have not reached the 'rest' (ירושלים), and you have not even reached the 'inheritance' (שילה).
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק is saying: Of course you have not reached the 'rest.' But you have not even reached the 'inheritance' either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמעון by explaining why the פסוק mentions ירושלים first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is a 'not only this, but even that' order, not a time order. Saying the people have not reached ירושלים is obvious, so the פסוק adds that they have not even reached שילה. This removes the challenge from step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means to say
It goes without saying
You have reached

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: מנוחה is שילה and נחלה is ירושלים, in time order. רבי שמעון: מנוחה is ירושלים and נחלה is שילה, read as 'not only have you not reached ירושלים, you have not even reached שילה.'
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי שמעון's version as a timeline. The פסוק goes from the bigger place to the smaller one, so ירושלים comes first even though שילה came first in history.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
It goes without saying that you have not reached the "rest"
phrases.notes: For רבי שמעון, the 'rest' is ירושלים.

phrases.english: but even the "inheritance" too
you have not reached.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא מְנוּחָה דְּלָא מְטֵיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 and keeps רבי שמעון's view standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the order of the פסוק as 'not only this, but even that'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק lists the places in time order, so the first one named must be שילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון the פסוק goes from greater to lesser: you have not reached ירושלים, and not even שילה.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל: both words mean שילה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that both מנוחה and נחלה refer to שילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: both this word and that word refer to שילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third opinion about the words מנוחה and נחלה in the פסוק. The school of רבי ישמעאל says both words point to the same place, שילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון each split the two words between two places. This view does not split them at all: both words describe שילה. So the פסוק is talking about one place only.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the study house of רבי ישמעאל
This and that, meaning both of them
Shiloh, where the משכן stood before the בית המקדש

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
This and that are Shiloh.
phrases.notes: "This and that" means both words from the פסוק, מנוחה and נחלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third reading of the פסוק after the views of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both מנוחה and נחלה refer to שילה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי: both words mean ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says both מנוחה and נחלה refer to ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: both this word and that word refer to ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth opinion. רבי שמעון בן יוחי says both words point to ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the school of רבי ישמעאל. Both views say the two words describe one place, but they disagree on which place. Now we have four views in total.

keyTerms.meaning: Jerusalem, where the בית המקדש stood

steps.whatToRemember: Four views: רבי יהודה (מנוחה is שילה, נחלה is ירושלים), רבי שמעון (the reverse), school of רבי ישמעאל (both are שילה), רבי שמעון בן יוחי (both are ירושלים).
steps.confusionAlert: Plain 'רבי שמעון' in step 18 is usually the same sage as רבי שמעון בן יוחי here. These are two different reports of his reading. In step 18 the two words are split between two places, and here both words mean ירושלים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says:
This and that are Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite single-place reading to the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both מנוחה and נחלה refer to ירושלים.

steps.title: Opening a question: it makes sense for the one who says מנוחה is a certain place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a בשלמא question: according to the one who says מנוחה is a certain place, the פסוק makes sense. The question continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the one who says that מנוחה is...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts saying "this works well for the one who says מנוחה means one specific place," and the rest of the question comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בשלמא opening first agrees that one view fits well, so that it can then ask why the other view does not. Which view is granted and which is challenged only becomes clear on the next amud. The school of רבי ישמעאל also says מנוחה is שילה, so we cannot tell yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense; opens a contrast question
According to the one who says
Rest, a word from the פסוק

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
"Rest," this is

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing all four views, the גמרא starts comparing them.
steps.kashyaTarget: The views that say both words mean one place (school of רבי ישמעאל and רבי שמעון בן יוחי).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two-place views explain why the פסוק uses two words, the single-place views must explain why it uses two words for one place. The full challenge continues in the next section.
